rules.title: Anti-Eviction Statute (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1)
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a residential tenant only on statutory grounds (e.g., nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, lease breaches, habitual late payment, retirement of property, condominium conversion, owner occupancy, certain criminal offenses), after the required Notice to Cease and/or Notice to Quit and a court judgment. Notice periods range from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground, and relocation assistance is required for some grounds.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit from 3 days up to 3 years by ground (e.g., 1 month for lease breach, 3 months for health/safety removal, 18 months for retiring property, 3 years for conversion); relocation of 6 times monthly rent for illegal occupancy
rules.penalty: Self-help evictions are illegal; the landlord may be liable for damages, court costs and attorney fees, and may be charged with disorderly conduct. Unpaid relocation accrues 18% annual interest and is a lien on the property.
rules.status_basis: Described as the statutory grounds in the Anti-Eviction Statute in the state's Landlord-Tenant guide.

exempt_if.text: owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings (landlord-occupied) are treated under separate removal rules

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental tenancies in New Jersey.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are handled under a separate, narrower set of grounds.
